findings.topic: legacy-arm residual escape hatch vs C2 all-routes-through-table
findings.message: C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms route through the single declarative table. The draft quietly redefines the phase gate as 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms', and Phase 7 permits closure with the remaining-legacy-arms counter 'driven to zero OR its residual explicitly carried as named debt'. 'Named debt' is not the documented North-Star amendment path — it is a unilateral criterion dilution pre-authorized inside the plan. A route with a table ROW whose bytes still execute through the legacy if-elif chain has not migrated; the in-branch import-shadowing class C2 also demands dead ('zero remain') survives in every unmigrated arm. Either commit to zero legacy arms as a hard C2 exit condition of the effort, or route the narrowing through the amendment path with John's approval NOW — the plan may not ship its own loophole.

findings.topic: pillar sequencing defers the highest-value pillars to last
findings.message: The bored-investor problem: Stage-0's own oranges framing ranks the event log as the highest-Butler-value pillar and names the supervisor split as the fix for John's REAL recurring pain (nssm restart kills in-flight Foreman runs), yet the plan lands them 5th and 6th of 7 phases, behind frontend extraction, route migration, and repo hygiene. If the effort stalls at 50% — the base case for multi-month re-architectures — John holds a smaller file and identical pain. The dependencies asserted to justify this are thin or fabricated: the journal instruments effort_history/session_registry/terminal_session/job_runner, none of which is blocked by the anchor_gui frontend blobs or the route table; the jobs-half supervisor is called 'low-risk, immediately delivers restart survival' by Stage-0 D2 itself and needs neither the journal (job_runner already has durable records + job-object + creation-time identity) nor 'IPC-adjacent auth' from the route table (loopback token IPC reuses paths.auth_ok directly). Only the data-dir move (journals born outside the repo) is a real ordering constraint. Re-sequence so at least one of C3/C4 (recommend the jobs-half supervisor) lands in the first half of the effort, or state honestly why value is being deferred.

findings.topic: Phase 0 packs planning work whose output can invalidate the locked plan
findings.message: Phase 0 defers to build-time ground truth that is cheap, mechanical, and knowable during planning — and whose answer gates the plan's own validity. The interpolation census in particular decides whether the C1 bar (≥7,000-line shrink, ~50-line blob cap) must be amended 'NOW, not mid-wave' — meaning the plan is being locked while explicitly anticipating an immediate amendment to its first success criterion. A grep-classifiable census over two known line ranges, the consumer-enumeration grep, the dependency DAG, and the three Butler user stories are all Stage-1/Stage-2 planning artifacts; running them DURING Stage 2 (before Foreman) resolves the C1 bar, the open-route consumer set, and the event-envelope validation target before anything is committed. As drafted, Phase 0 is ~12 deliverables spanning two spikes, a Playwright suite, a tripwire harness, a deploy shim, process rituals, and a freeze protocol — a whole sub-project labeled 'instrumentation' with no sizing, delaying all user-visible value behind it. Pull the paper artifacts into Stage 2; keep Phase 0 to the two spikes, the Playwright flows, and the tripwire.

findings.topic: journal emit() failure semantics unspecified under journal-first ordering
findings.message: The plan decrees emit-event-THEN-write-legacy at every mutation-of-record, but never specifies what happens when emit() itself FAILS (disk full, schema-validation bug, lock contention, a malformed payload from one of ~10 instrumented subsystems). If emit() raising blocks the legacy write, a journal bug takes down the authoritative store path across session lifecycle, jobs, grass, and deliverables simultaneously — inverting D1 ('legacy stores stay authoritative') and violating C7, with the blast radius of the one choke point the design celebrates. The off-switch flag is a human-latency remedy, not a failure semantic. The plan must state the rule: emit() is fail-open with respect to the legacy write (log + counter + healthcheck surface on journal-write failure; legacy write ALWAYS proceeds), and the parity gate's classification must include 'legacy-ahead-because-emit-failed' as distinguishable from the BUG class.

findings.topic: no sizing, duration, or wave-count estimates anywhere in the plan
findings.message: Seven phases, roughly sixty near-term specifics, two spikes, four new healthcheck walks, a second NSSM service — and not one phase carries a size, wave count, or rough duration. The investor cannot judge whether the Phase-0 front-load pays back, whether the extraction merge-freeze window is days or weeks (it must be coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build, which needs a real window, not 'a soft freeze'), or whether the plan fits any horizon at all. C7's no-multi-day-freeze and never-broken-increment clauses are unverifiable without at least coarse per-phase sizing and an explicit statement of what gets CUT first if the effort must shrink. A FULL-pipeline Stage-1 master plan should rank the phases by value-per-cost and mark the minimum shippable subset (per the North Star: jobs-half C4 is non-negotiable; C1's bar is amendable) — this draft treats all seven phases as equally mandatory and unpriced.

findings.topic: Phase-0 'no runtime change' claim contradicted by the contract shim, which also references a not-yet-existing ANCHOR_BOOT
findings.message: Phase 0's framing paragraph claims 'Nothing here changes runtime behavior, so C7 risk is near zero', yet one of its own deliverables ships a frontend↔backend contract shim to the LIVE service: ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, the server 409s a mismatch. That is a client+server behavior change with its own stale-tab failure modes — exactly the class it exists to prevent. Worse, window.ANCHOR_BOOT does not exist until the Phase-1 extraction introduces the bootstrap JSON; in Phase 0 the build id must ride the still-embedded f-string, meaning the shim is built twice or the plan's dependency arrow is backwards. State honestly that Phase 0 contains one behavior-bearing deploy, and specify the pre-extraction carrier for the build id.

findings.topic: tripwire enumeration mode vs permanent enforcement mode conflated
findings.section: Phase 1 (Phase 0) write-site tripwire / Phase 5 completeness gate
findings.message: Phase 0 says the tripwire 'fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event' and 'stays on forever' — but no journal exists until Phase 5, so between Phase 0 and Phase 5 the tripwire in failing mode would redden the entire suite. It plainly needs two modes (enumerate/report in Phases 0–4, enforce from Phase 5), yet the plan never says so, nor who owns the allowlist of legitimately-unjournaled writes (per-tick/telemetry 'excluded BY RULE' — which rule, checked where?) as the codebase drifts between the two phases. Specify the mode switch, its flip point, and the allowlist's review discipline, or the C3 completeness gate is a gate only in narrative.

findings.topic: parity-gate tail tolerance vs C3's 'zero divergence'
findings.message: C3 requires the parity gate to report ZERO divergence; the draft's gate 'tolerates a bounded tail window of recent events' and classifies journal-ahead as OK. Reasonable engineering for a live 5AM run, but as written it is a weaker predicate than the criterion. Make the two-tier structure explicit: the TEST-suite parity gate runs quiescent and asserts literal zero divergence (the C3 bar), while the live healthcheck run applies the bounded-tail classification with journal-ahead-within-window as the only tolerated class — and any legacy-ahead or conflict is a hard failure in both tiers. Otherwise the scorecard will mark C3 'met' against a diluted definition.

findings.topic: '20× nightly' soak infrastructure does not exist and is unowned
findings.message: The plan repeatedly invokes a rule that each new healthcheck walk 'runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run', but the host has exactly one scheduled run (5AM) — there is no nightly-repetition harness, no scheduled task for it, and no phase deliverable that builds one. Four new walks (journal parity, supervisor probes, cookie/auth, relocated-data-dir) are gated on this nonexistent infrastructure. Either name the harness as a Phase-0/Phase-6 deliverable (a second scheduled task + a repetition report) or replace the rule with something the current infrastructure can enforce.

Every section is double-numbered ('Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — …'), so the ConPTY-spike directive ('early'), cross-references like 'Phase-3 event envelope' (which is Phase 5's content under the outer numbering), and any Foreman wave mapping are ambiguous by one everywhere. Pick one numbering before Stage 2 or the implementation plan will inherit off-by-one references.

The preamble asserts 'All 52 integrated ideas are absorbed' and specifics cite opaque tags (Integrated 1..52, Mitigation 1..20) that appear nowhere in the North Star or the visible research input, so neither the Sharks nor the Judge can verify absorption or spot a silently dropped idea. Attach the numbered idea/mitigation ledger as a plan appendix or drop the claim.
